featured_reviews.name: Krittika Khandare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review to document a serious food safety incident at PVR, Jio World Plaza, BKC.

On 15 January 2026, I attended the 6:00 PM show of Avatar 3 in Audi 6. Before the movie, I purchased food from the PVR counter. While eating it during the show, the final bite contained a visible piece of glass that entered my mouth. I immediately spat it out. The fact that I was not physically injured was purely a matter of luck, this could have caused severe internal injury or worse.

I have video evidence clearly showing the glass shard in the food.

What has been equally disturbing is the way this matter has been handled since. Despite multiple emails, follow-ups, and assurances that the issue was being taken seriously, there were significant delays, inconsistent communication, and ultimately a response stating that no lapse could be established at their end. The only gesture initially offered was complimentary movie tickets, which is entirely inappropriate for a life-threatening food safety incident.

As a paying customer, being exposed to such a risk and then experiencing weeks of delay and deflection has been deeply distressing. This review is being posted so that other patrons are aware and so that this concern is documented publicly after private escalation failed to lead to a responsible resolution.

I hope PVR reviews its food safety accountability and customer handling practices more seriously going forward.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Jio PVR recently for an evening weekday show. The theatre itself was extremely clean, the seats were very comfortable, and the cooling was VERY strong — honestly, carry a jacket if you’re planning to watch a movie there because it gets quite cold inside. The overall ambience and maintenance were excellent.

Ticket pricing between ₹250–₹500 feels reasonable considering the cleanliness and comfort, especially if booked smartly on weekdays.

But as usual with PVR, the food pricing is absurd. Ordered a ₹350 Schezwan Paneer Wrap and it was a complete waste of money. The taste was terrible and definitely not worth the price. They serve it properly with a tray, plate, and cutlery, but realistically, how convenient is that setup inside a movie theatre while watching a film in the dark?

Popcorn and drinks are also heavily overpriced, and the quantity doesn’t justify the cost either.

Overall: great theatre experience for seating, cleanliness, and ambience — but avoid spending too much on the food unless you’re okay paying premium prices for average quality.

featured_reviews.name: Jay Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: I wish there was a zero-star option on Google because this was a truly horrible experience at Cinepolis Magnet Mall, Bhandup. I, Jay, went to watch the movie "Obsession" with my friend. Another friend had booked the tickets but couldn't make it due to a personal reason. He gave us the ticket QR screenshot, and Vikas Jha, the watchman, checked it and let us in. However, before the interval, we were stopped three times inside the cinema by different Cinepolis executives—Anuyog, Nagesh, and another. We kept showing them the ticket. But during the interval, Anuyog dragged me outside, insisting the ticket was invalid. I had him contact BookMyShow support, who confirmed the ticket was legitimate. Still, Cinepolis did nothing to help. We were told to leave mid-movie, and they asked us to pay again directly to them for a new ticket. The way Anuyog and Nagesh treated us was disgraceful. After returning home, I had to raise a formal complaint with BookMyShow, who thankfully issued a refund. But Cinepolis, you have a long way to go. Stay away if you value a hassle-free cinema experience.

HI Jay,
Thank you for taking the time to share your detailed feedback. We sincerely regret to learn about the inconvenience and distress caused during your recent visit.
Please note that our teams are required to verify tickets in accordance with established procedures to ensure a secure and seamless experience for all guests. However, we are concerned to learn that the matter was not resolved in a manner that met your expectations and that your interaction with our team left you dissatisfied.

We regret any inconvenience caused and appreciate you bringing this matter to our attention. Your feedback regarding the ticket verification process, the handling of the situation, and the overall guest experience. Reach out to us at support@cinepolis.com with your contact number along with the screenshot of this review for corrective actions.
 We are committed to continuously improving our service standards and ensuring a better experience for our guests.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sound system and screen size is top notch.
It has 6 auditoriums.
The 6th one has a weird seating arrangement. Even after sitting in H row in 6th Audi, you'll be very close to the screen. The seats are very irritating because there is no mechanism to adjust their position. Your neck will pain and body aches. It really hurts.
Eatables and drinks are as usual overpriced.

It is basically on 3rd floor inside a newly opened mall where mostly outlets are not yet sold. The escalators do not operate fully functional. Have to opt for lift anyhow which is again just at the centre with a lot of waiting time.
Air conditioning inside the auditoriums is excellent.
Saturdays and Sundays are mostly crowded.
Prefer auditorium 3 over 6 in any case.
You can use your wisdom while booking online seeing the seats arrangement and pattern.
Lots of advertisements will be played before starting a movie.
Interval is around 15 min which is quite a standard protocol.
Parking is available in the basement for the entire mall.
It is the best available option near Bhandup area. If you are an IITian, go for it anyday.

featured_reviews.review_text:
To begin with, finding the theatre was quite confusing. There were no boards, signs, or posters indicating that a theatre was located there. My cab dropped me right in front of the building, but I still couldn’t see any clear markings to confirm I was at the right place.

Next, after completing the ticket check and heading upstairs, I noticed there were very few seats available for waiting. Only about ten people could sit on a sofa, and the rest had to stand until roughly ten minutes before the show began. So, if you arrive early, be prepared to wait standing.

Another issue — (Screen 2) avoid seats D19 and D20 in the upper section. Your view will be blocked by a gypsum board placed directly in front.

The seating overall is not very comfortable, especially for back support. The sound quality was also below expectations, lacking smoothness and clarity.

Like in many theatres, disturbances were present: people searching for seats with mobile flashlights after the movie started, crying babies, phone conversations, latecomers, people recording videos, and vendors distributing popcorn mid-show etc.

Speaking of popcorn — I paid ₹460 for one serving and ₹70 for a half-litre bottle of mineral water. Including my travel, I spent around ₹1,500 just to watch a movie.

Finally, a serious safety concern: when exiting after the show, you must use the stairs. Some steps are partially damaged, making it risky to walk in a crowd. Today, I even witnessed a man fall while carrying a small child because of the broken steps. Please be cautious.

I visited Miraj Cinemas: IMAX, Wadala in the morning to watch Avatar: Fire and Ash, and overall, it was a really good experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar shelke
featured_reviews.review_text:
📍 Miraj Cinemas Wadala

Miraj Cinemas Wadala is a very good place to watch movies in IMAX and offers one of the best cinema experiences in India. It is known for housing India’s largest IMAX screen, which makes the overall viewing experience truly grand and immersive. The massive screen delivers sharp visuals, vibrant colors, and excellent clarity, making every scene feel larger than life.

I watched Avatar: Fire and Ash here, and the experience was outstanding. The visuals looked absolutely stunning on the huge IMAX screen, and the depth and details of every scene were clearly visible. The powerful sound system made the movie even more immersive, allowing you to feel every background score, action sequence, and dialogue perfectly. Watching a visually rich movie like Avatar in this IMAX theatre truly takes the cinematic experience to another level.

The seating is comfortable and well arranged, providing a clear view of the screen from almost every seat. The ambience of the theatre is modern, clean, and well maintained. Staff members are polite, and entry and exit are well managed. The food and beverage options are good, though slightly expensive, which is expected in an IMAX theatre.

Overall, Miraj Cinemas Wadala is an excellent destination for movie lovers who want to enjoy films in IMAX format. Highly recommended for a premium and memorable movie-watching experience. 🎬🍿

featured_reviews.name: Ashish
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to watch O'Romeo on Screen 2. There are 4 other screens. This review is not about the largest IMAX screen in dome shaped theatre because mostly English movies are shown in that.
This cinema hall deserves 5 star rating literally considering its overall experience. The ambience is super clean. The washroom area is neat and clean with facilities such as hand drier, napkins stand, liquid hand wash, plants etc. The lighting is superb everywhere in and out. Photogenic space everywhere around with benches, sofas, Chandelier, etc.
The screen size, sound quality, AC temperature, visual quality, cleanliness, etc. everything is top class. I booked recliner seat. It is button operated offering a space to keep the glass and a tray to keep eatables, handkerchief, mobile etc. Ladies purse or totte bag is allowed inside the hall. The staff is polite. The hall is cleaned immediately after the movie is over before the next show.
The food court has a lot of options and considering the quality of ambience and slow relaxing music inside the premises, the pricing is justified.
Free clean drinking water is available with disposable paper cups.
The crowd is also decent.
Generally, the cinema hall is almost empty for most of the Bollywood movies; hence, one can enjoy solitude also many a times.
They appreciate online payments and cards at food courts and booking box office counter. Lot of food options are available such as samosa, nachos, popcorn, pizza, burger, etc.
Frisking process is very smooth.
Valet parking is available.
It is at a walking distance from Bhakti Park Monorail station. There is a metro station under construction nearby.
Beside IMAX, one can enjoy a very clean green 25 acres Bhakti Park.
There is car racing nearby as well.

featured_reviews.name: Jigar Budhdev
featured_reviews.review_text: This is the best IMAX experience in India. The dome shaped structure means you're looking down the screen if you're seated at the back. This really helps. There's ample parking since this is a standalone multiplex and not part of any mall. My recent experience at the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand in Dadar left me with mixed feelings. While the overall service of the Shivneri buses remains commendable, the facilities at the bus stand itself are in dire need of improvement, particularly when it comes to providing adequate shelter and comfort for passengers.

On a rainy day, I found myself at the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand, eagerly waiting for my bus. Unfortunately, my anticipation was quickly dampened, both literally and figuratively, as the facility failed to offer proper protection from the elements. The absence of sufficient shelter made it difficult for passengers to find a dry spot to stand or sit, leaving many of us exposed to the rain. It was disheartening to see elderly passengers and families with children struggling to stay dry while waiting for their buses.

The lack of proper infrastructure at the bus stand was evident. The limited seating arrangements were inadequate for the number of passengers present, and those available were often wet due to the rain. There were no covered waiting areas or even basic shelters to shield passengers from the weather. This situation is particularly concerning during the monsoon season when rain is frequent and heavy in Mumbai. A bus stand as busy and important as Dadar's Shivneri should certainly prioritize the comfort and convenience of its passengers by providing better infrastructure.

Despite these shortcomings, there are several positive aspects to note about the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand. The staff at the stand were courteous and helpful, assisting passengers with their queries and providing timely updates about bus arrivals and departures. The ticketing process was efficient, and I appreciated the digital screens displaying real-time information about bus schedules. This helped in reducing the anxiety of waiting, as passengers could see exactly when their buses were expected to arrive.

Additionally, the cleanliness of the bus stand was maintained reasonably well. Despite the rain, the staff made efforts to keep the area free of litter, which is commendable. The security presence was also reassuring, ensuring that passengers felt safe while waiting for their buses.

However, the positive aspects cannot entirely overshadow the critical need for better facilities. For an otherwise excellent service like Shivneri, enhancing the infrastructure at the Dadar bus stand is essential. Investing in covered waiting areas, more seating, and improved drainage systems to prevent waterlogging would greatly enhance the passenger experience, especially during the rainy season.

In conclusion, while the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand in Dadar excels in terms of service efficiency, cleanliness, and staff courtesy, it falls short in providing basic facilities to protect passengers from adverse weather conditions. Addressing these issues will ensure that passengers have a comfortable and pleasant experience, regardless of the weather.

featured_reviews.review_text:
🎬 INOX IMAX – R City Mall, Ghatkopar | Honest IMAX Experience Review

I recently watched an IMAX screening at INOX IMAX R City Mall, and here’s a clear, no-nonsense review based on the actual experience.

Overall Experience: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5)

What Works Well:
•	IMAX scale & immersion: The auditorium delivers the signature IMAX feel with a massive screen and powerful surround sound, making it a good choice for big-budget, visually heavy films.
•	Comfortable environment: The hall is clean, well-maintained, and acoustics are solid, especially for action and background scores.
•	Location advantage: Being inside R City Mall makes it convenient with ample food and parking options.

What Could Be Better:
•	Projection quality (3D): While watching Avatar: Fire and Ash in 3D, the visuals felt noticeably blurred. A laser IMAX projection would have significantly improved sharpness, brightness, and depth.
•	Seats: The seating is decent but not premium. For long IMAX movies, better cushioning and ergonomics would enhance comfort.
•	3D clarity: Fast-moving scenes lacked crispness, which slightly broke immersion—something you don’t expect from an IMAX-branded screen.

Final Verdict:
INOX IMAX R City Mall is good for IMAX movies, especially if you value screen size and sound, but it falls short of a true next-gen IMAX experience due to the non-laser projection and average seating. Upgrade to laser projection and better seats, and this could easily become one of Mumbai’s top IMAX destinations.

Recommended for: Big action / spectacle films
Not ideal for: Viewers sensitive to 3D blur or expecting laser-sharp visuals

featured_reviews.name: Dev Sai
featured_reviews.review_text:
My visit to INOX Neelyog in Ghatkopar East was a bit of a mixed experience. While the theatre itself is okay, it feels like a bit of a deserted venue. The mall it’s located in is quite old, and despite being owned by PVR-INOX, the place feels stuck in time, lacking the modern amenities you’d expect from their brand. It doesn’t have the same fresh, updated atmosphere as other PVR-INOX theatres.

Its proximity to the Ghatkopar Railway Station makes it a convenient choice for moviegoers relying on public transport.

The seating was decent, but there was nothing exceptional about it. The overall maintenance seemed lacking, and the place just felt a bit neglected. The staff were polite, but the overall service felt a bit lackluster, especially when compared to other PVR-INOX theatres. The staff seemed understaffed, and there were minor delays in service, particularly at the concession stand. As for maintenance, it was evident that the theatre could use some attention. The cleanliness in the common areas and washrooms was below par, and the seats, though functional, showed signs of wear and tear.

The ticket prices were reasonable, but when compared to other PVR-INOX theatres, this one doesn’t justify the price for the experience it offers. Snacks were also the standard fare, but the portions were smaller, and they didn’t feel as fresh.

In summary, while it wasn’t a terrible experience, it felt more like a theatre stuck in the past, lacking the vibrant and well-maintained vibe you’d expect from a PVR-INOX property. It’s good if you're in the area, but I wouldn’t go out of my way for it.

featured_reviews.name: Venkat Krishnan
featured_reviews.review_text: I saw it from outside and came to know what would be inside. I was a resident of Chembur from 1960 to 1991. I still remember, during the 60s, it was pride of Chembur as it was the only air conditioned  theatre in the area and going there to watch any movie with family and friends was a great pleasure for all. AC was very powerful, seats very comfortable, picture and sound quality excellent, canteen used to serve tasty samosas, snacks and beverages at reasonable prices. Management was talking pains to maintain the ambience and decor. But over the period, due to poor management, improper maintenance, the quality deteriorated gradually and it has come to the present stage. Added to all these, competition from multiplexes has caused further damage. Most surprising is still it continues to run against all odds is something great. I doubt will there be any scope for improvement. The best option will be to sell the land to some potential builder who can build Shopping mall or residential tower, as the place is strategically located (very close to railway station and bus stop ). featured_reviews.name: Dev Sai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fun Cinemas, located on the 4th floor of K Star Mall in Chembur, offers a standard movie-going experience with some notable positives and areas that could use improvement. One of the standout aspects of this theatre is its diverse language screenings, including Tamil, Malayalam, Telugu, Hindi, and English. This makes it a great option for regional movie lovers in Mumbai who want to catch films in their native language.

The sound and visual quality are commendable, with Dolby Atmos enhancing the audio experience and the screen clarity being satisfactory. These technical aspects ensure that the core movie-watching experience is enjoyable. The theatre is also conveniently located near Diamond Garden and is close to Ghatala railway station, making it easily accessible for locals and commuters.

However, the theatre's location in an old and mostly abandoned mall detracts significantly from the overall experience. The mall feels deserted, especially at night, which creates an eerie and isolated atmosphere. Inside, the seating, although slightly repaired and improved, is still average, with some chairs showing signs of wear and tear. The maintenance of the premises is also below par, with cleanliness in common areas needing much more attention.

The food and beverage options are decent, with the nachos and cool drinks standing out as personal favorites. However, like most multiplexes in Mumbai, the prices are high, which doesn’t always align with the quality or portion sizes. There have also been occasional complaints about stale food, which is disappointing.

In conclusion, Fun Cinemas in K Star Mall is a decent choice if you’re looking to watch movies in regional languages or live nearby. However, the outdated ambiance, maintenance issues, and high prices make it a less appealing option compared to other multiplexes in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very good cinema hall for normal movie-goers. The theatre is clean, comfortable, and well-maintained.
The sound quality is clear and powerful, giving a good Dolby-like surround experience for most movies. Screen brightness and picture clarity are also nice.

The best part is the location — it’s very close to Chinchpokli railway station, so travelling is super easy. Staff behaviour is decent and ticket prices are affordable.

If you're looking for a good cinema with clean ambience, nice sound effect, and easy railway access, Jaihind is a great choice.

featured_reviews.review_text: Very disappointing experience. The seats were in poor condition, uncomfortable, and not worth the ticket price. The food and beverages were extremely overpriced for the quality offered. Hygiene standards also seemed lacking, especially around the seating area. Overall, the theatre does not provide value for money, and management should pay more attention to seat maintenance, cleanliness, and customer comfort. I would not recommend this theatre until these issues are addressed.

featured_reviews.name: Buddy Caprice
featured_reviews.review_text: Old world nostalgia to this place! Seats are not on an incline so ensure you book seats in the front. They have renovated it quite well. Food and beverage options are amlle and we got a food coupon for ₹300 when we entered here for a movie that includes a pizza, cold coffee and popcorn. The taste was good and value for money. Restrooms were well maintained. The screen accessibility was a little weird to understand and lifts were smaller than usual so lot of people kept waiting and crowding. Sound system also could use an upgrade and screen needs a revamp too for crisper brighter colors. 3D experience wasn't as good as for a PVR or Inox but for the price it was manageable.

featured_reviews.name: PURVA MEVADA
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience at Mukta Jaihind Cinema, especially Screen 1. The theatre claims to be upgraded, but it feels like only the exterior has changed while the inside is still poorly maintained.
The seats were uncomfortable and itchy, the carpets were dusty, and there was leftover popcorn under the seats, showing a complete lack of cleanliness. The sound system was extremely loud to the point of causing ear pain, and the speakers sounded damaged and tearing apart during the movie.
The housekeeping staff seemed untrained, and the overall experience felt very lethargic and badly managed. For the ticket prices they charge, basic hygiene and maintenance should at least be taken seriously.
I would not recommend this theatre unless they seriously improve the upkeep and customer experience.
